Source: Anarchs Guide

The Anarch Movement is not a sect in the formal sense but a loose, borderless fellowship of vampires bound by a shared conviction: that the elder-dominated hierarchies of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} are unjust tyrannies over the young. Its founding ideal is libertas - the free will owed to every Kindred regardless of age or generation - and its origin lies in the Anarch Revolt, when Spanish @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} neonates, led by Patricia Tyler, rose against elders who had abandoned them to the Inquisition rather than honor their obligations under the Lex Talionis. The revolt spread through @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} Italy and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} Eastern Europe before it was checked by the elders' own countermeasure: the formation of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}. Anarchs still speak of the Convention of Thorns that ended the Revolt not as a peace but as a surrender, one that returned them to servitude under their sires and, in the bargain, produced both the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} and, through the defectors who refused its terms, the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}.

Anarchs have never abandoned the dream that flickered briefly during the Victorian Age and blazed again in 1944, when Jeremy MacNeil, Salvador Garcia, and their allies overthrew the corrupt Prince of Los Angeles in the Second Anarch Revolt and declared the Anarch Free State, a stretch of California governed by no prince or primogen. The Free State adopted the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference.JournalEntry.St7uVm2DqK4nRy8X]{Status} Perfectus, a charter calling on anarchs everywhere to care for one another across clan lines and extend freedom to all Kindred. It endured for decades before collapsing under internal gang warfare and a Cathayan divide-and-conquer campaign at the end of the millennium - a fate anarchs read less as defeat than as proof that the Movement survives any single setback, since new discontents always rise to take up the cause.

Where the Camarilla imposes princes and primogen by decree and the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} enforces obedience through the blood bond of the Vaulderie, anarch authority exists only by consent. The basic social unit is the gang (sometimes called a coterie or pack), a cross-clan band that claims a stretch of turf, called a barony, and looks after its own. In contested cities, gangs often defer to a single charismatic baron, a "first among equals" who mediates disputes between factions but holds no authority beyond what his personal standing commands. In stronger, more established communities - Anarch Free Territories - power is more often vested in a representative council, with seats apportioned by gang or peer group rather than by clan, a structure anarchs pointedly distinguish from the Camarilla's primogen councils. Some radicals reject even this much structure, preferring open popular assemblies where every interested vampire has a voice in each decision, a purer expression of consensus but one that can leave a community slow to react to outside threats.

Beneath the barons and councils runs a rotating cast of unofficial "officers" - ambassadors who treat with princes and bishops on the community's behalf, counters who track who comes and goes, deputies or sentinels who muster to defend the territory, and moles who slip into enemy domains to gather warning of attack. None of these roles confer status; among anarchs, respect earns the job, not the reverse, and a leader who forgets this is quickly abandoned by the people who once followed him.

The Movement's culture is one of restless tension between its egalitarian ideals and the hard practicalities of survival: freedom without structure breeds vulnerability, yet any structure risks recreating the very tyranny anarchs fled. Gangs feud over turf and old grudges even as they unite instinctively against Camarilla or Sabbat incursions, and individual anarchs are prized less for clan or generation than for what they contribute to the Cause. Whatever their failures, anarchs remain committed to the belief that a Kindred's worth should be judged by character alone - and that the fight for that ideal, however many times it is crushed, will always be taken up again.

Standing Between the Sects: Under the terms of the Convention of Thorns, true anarchs occupy a strange legal limbo shared by no other Kindred: they hold no @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference.JournalEntry.St7uVm2DqK4nRy8X]{Status} among either the Camarilla or the Sabbat, not even the barest acknowledgement, and cannot ever earn any within those sects' hierarchies. In exchange, they cannot be summoned before sect justice or hunted on mere say-so, and their disregard for elders' authority carries no formal penalty. The arrangement cuts both ways, however - Kindred owe anarchs no boons, hospitality, or protection, and many princes are only too happy to use wandering anarchs as convenient scapegoats when things go wrong in a city, treaty or no treaty.

Beyond the Stereotype: The popular image of the anarch - a howling neonate covered in piercings, torching a prince's rose garden between bouts of ghoul-beating - is a caricature few true anarchs actually resemble. Anarchs are drawn from every clan and generation, and what unites them is not fashion or temper but a refusal to accept the entire bargain the sects offer: training, protection, and status in exchange for submission to elder rule. A true anarch would rather face Final Death than kneel to those who claim authority by blood alone, and many carry the scars of that choice - reputations for Notoriety, estranged sires, clan enmity, or a lingering Sire's Resentment that follows them from city to city.

The Anarch Free States: The movement's greatest modern foothold remains the West Coast of the United States, where the fall of the Los Angeles prince metastasized into a broader "Anarch Free State" stretching along nearly the entire coastline and inland, bounded by Sabbat-held Mexico to the south and interrupted only by Camarilla-held San Francisco, which has never fallen despite being surrounded on nearly all sides.
